name: Leutascher Geisterklamm
kurzbeschreibung: The Leutascher Geisterklamm: a spectacular rock gorge on the Bavarian border featuring a 970 m steel walkway, bold panoramic bridge, and goblin trail.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Leutascher Geisterklamm (also known as the Leutaschklamm) is a spectacular, deeply incised rock gorge situated directly on the border between the Tyrolean high plateau of Leutasch/Seefeld and the Bavarian market town of Mittenwald. Rushing through the narrow valley, the untamed Leutascher Ache has carved its way deep into the hard Wetterstein limestone over millennia. Since its grand opening in 2006, this cross-border ravine has been celebrated as a masterpiece of Alpine trail engineering, captivating families, geology enthusiasts, and hikers with an audacious, seemingly floating footbridge system suspended directly above roaring whitewater torrents.

Gorge Walkway & Panoramic Bridge

The development of this previously inaccessible natural canyon was realised as a joint Austrian-German EU project. The absolute crowning attraction is the 970-metre-long Klammgeistweg: a daring walkway constructed of galvanized steel gratings and sturdy safety railings, anchored horizontally straight into sheer rock faces rising up to 100 metres high. Looking down through the open mesh decking, walkers gaze directly into swirling potholes and the sparkling emerald-green pools of the mountain river. The midpoint of the route is the stunning Panoramabrücke: suspended at a dizzying height of around 50 metres, this steel suspension footbridge spans the chasm, commanding breathtaking views of the rugged Wettersteingebirge and the peaks of the Karwendel. For young explorers, the themed loop has been conceived as the mystical realm of the "Gorge Spirit": across 40 interactive discovery and listening stations, gorge goblins and water sprites explain glacial polish, geological wonders, and the secrets of Alpine water. At the lower Bavarian end of the gorge near Mittenwald, a shorter, privately operated Wasserfallsteig leads to a thundering 23-metre-high waterfall.

Visit & Getting There

The Klammgeistweg and the Panoramabrücke are open around the clock daily and are free of charge during snow-free months from early May to late October/November (officially closed by authorities during winter ice, snow, or extreme weather). Optional admission to the small waterfall path near Mittenwald costs around €4.00 for adults. Arrival by car: From Seefeld in Tirol along the L14 through the Leutaschtal to the hamlet of Schanz (large pay-and-display hikers' car park located directly at the trail entrance). Alternatively, access from Mittenwald via P1/P2 Klamm car parks. By public transport: ÖBB/S-Bahn train to Seefeld in Tirol station, from where regional VVT bus line 430 runs through the Leutaschtal directly to the Leutasch Schanz bus stop.

Tips

The steel grating walkway is largely level and wide enough for two-way pedestrian traffic, though it does require a head for heights; due to individual steps and open grating floors, it is only conditionally suitable for standard prams and wheelchairs (dogs are permitted on leashes, though many four-legged companions shy away from the see-through metal grids). Allow approximately 1.5 to 2 hours of walking time for the complete circuit over the suspension bridge. After your hike, the traditional Gasthof Zur Schanze invites you to recharge with hearty Tyrolean dumpling soups and refreshments.
